author: kyleboas
body:
### Motivation
- LLM API calls sometimes fail with transient upstream/internal server errors (e.g. `500`) that should be retried like rate-limit responses to improve robustness.
- The existing retry logic only retried `429`/`529` but missed other transient HTTP statuses that are commonly recoverable.

### Description
- Added `isRetryableLlmStatus(status: number)` in `src/llm.ts` to centralize which HTTP statuses are retryable (includes `408`, `429`, `500-504`, `529`).
- Switched the retry check in `callLLM` to use `isRetryableLlmStatus(...)` while preserving exponential backoff via `LLM_OVERLOAD_RETRY_BASE_MS` and `LLM_OVERLOAD_RETRY_MAX`.
- Added a unit test in `src/llm.test.ts` that verifies a `500` response is retried and then succeeds on the next attempt.
- No changes to public API shape or retry limits were made.

### Testing
- Ran typecheck with `npm run typecheck` and it succeeded.
- Ran unit tests with `npx vitest run src/llm.test.ts --config vitest.local.config.ts` (temporary Node environment config) and `src/llm.test.ts` passed (10 tests passed).
- Attempting to run the full `npx vitest` in the default Cloudflare Worker environment surfaced an unrelated runtime binding issue (`SANDBOX` service missing), so a local Node test config was used to validate the change.

This PR adds a user setting for immediate rendering, on MacOS and Linux. I saw noticeable improvements on MacOS 14.8.3 with Apple Silicon. I haven’t been able to manually test on Linux due to GPU virtualization issues. On my Windows VM I didn’t notice any rendering latency to begin with.

I’m happy to refine as needed.

Possibly related to #26900.

author: dirkwa
body:
## Problem

PR #2342 added an explicit GET route for `/@signalk/server-admin-ui-react19/` to inject addon scripts into `index.html`. However, Express compiles route patterns like `/path/` with an optional trailing slash (`\/?`), so the handler also matches `/@signalk/server-admin-ui-react19` (without slash). Since this route is registered before `webapps.js` mounts `express.static`, it intercepts the request and serves `index.html` at the slash-less URL — causing the browser to resolve relative asset paths against the wrong base, resulting in 404s for all static assets.

## Fix

- Add an explicit 301 redirect in the `/admin/` and `/@signalk/server-admin-ui-react19/` GET handlers when the trailing slash is missing, restoring the behaviour `express.static` would have provided
- No redundant routes or `express.static` mounts needed — `webapps.js` already handles static file serving
- Update the `apps/list` API endpoint to return webapp locations with trailing slashes
- Update `urlToWebapp()` in both admin UIs to generate trailing-slash URLs, eliminating the redirect hop when clicking a webapp

## Tested
- Manual tests on AMD64 and ARM64 with and without installing new webapps and embedded R16 webapps in R19

author: copilot
body:
Starters in the expanded lineup detail rows were not displaying in the correct positional order. The liveScoring API returns players in arbitrary order; no sort was applied.

## Changes

- **Position-based sort** — starters are sorted by a fixed position priority list before rendering:
  ```js
  var POS_ORDER = ['QB','RB','WR','TE','PK','DT','DE','LB','CB','S'];
  ```
  Positions not in the list sort to the end.

- **Default CORS proxy URL** — hardcoded to `https://mfl-proxy-worker.kartsetupelite.workers.dev/` unconditionally, replacing the `window.location.origin` fallback logic.

author: fisheepy
body:
### Motivation
- Remove the `react-spring` dependency and simplify animation/gesture handling to avoid heavy animation library transitive conflicts and make interactions easier to reason about. 
- Provide a standalone technical analysis in Chinese for the app to capture architecture, risks and migration recommendations.

### Description
- Removed `useSpring`/`animated` usage and import sites and replaced them with local React state (`useState`) and CSS `transform`/`transition` driven movement in `src/messageDetailComponent.js` to implement horizontal swipe-to-back behavior. 
- Replaced the animated pull-down region in `src/notificationModal.js` with a `dragY` state and inline `transform`/`transition` styles to implement pull-to-refresh visual feedback, and added `isDragging` flags to disable transitions while dragging. 
- Updated `useDrag` handlers in both components to manage movement via state (`dragX`/`dragY`) and to trigger `onBack` or set `isPulledDown` when thresholds are met. 
- Added a new documentation file `APP_ANALYSIS_ZH.md` containing a comprehensive Chinese-language technical analysis, deployment guidance, risk assessment and a migration plan to remove `react-spring` safely.

### Testing
- No automated tests were run against these changes in this rollout.

Title, description

body:
## Summary

Implements the Personality Logging Effect Node (OMN-2575, Part I of the Quirks epic). This is a fully independent deliverable — no dependencies on other Quirks tickets.

### What's delivered

- **`ModelLogEvent`** — canonical structured log event (severity, event_name, message, attrs, metrics, trace, policy)
- **`ModelPersonalityProfile`** — phrase-pack-driven rendering profile; built-in: `default`, `deadpan`, `panic_comic`
- **`ModelRenderedLog`** — output of PersonalityAdapter with immutable original event reference
- **`ModelLoggingConfig`** — YAML-backed runtime config (routing rules, throttle, quiet hours, privacy mode)
- **`PersonalityAdapter`** — pure deterministic transformation: same input + same profile = identical output
- **`StdoutSink`** — level-filtered stdout output
- **`SlackSink`** — Block Kit format with metrics fields and trace context; token-bucket rate limiter (max_per_minute), 5-minute dedup window keyed on event_name + attrs hash, quiet hours suppression
- **`JsonSink`** — newline-delimited JSON of raw LogEvent (personality rendering bypassed)
- **`NodePersonalityLoggingEffect`** — ONEX Effect Node; glob routing rules, strict privacy redaction, asyncio queue ingestion, `process_one()` API
- **`LiveConfigLoader`** — watchfiles-based live config reload; switch personality profile without restart

### Design invariants

- Personality rendering NEVER mutates `LogEvent.attrs` or any structured field
- `privacy_mode: strict` applies redaction before any rendering
- Sink failures NEVER propagate to callers
- Rendering is fully deterministic (no random selection)

## Test plan

- [x] 19 unit tests: determinism x100, all severity levels, all built-in profiles, redaction patterns, custom profile registration
- [x] 4 integration-style tests (mocked HTTP): Block Kit payload structure, quiet hours suppression, full pipeline routing, strict redaction
- [x] Mypy strict — 355 source files, 0 errors
- [x] ruff format + check — 0 issues
- [x] pre-commit all hooks — passed
- [x] Full unit suite — 1756 passed, 0 failures

Closes OMN-2575

## Summary

- Adds a `[!WARNING]` callout making it explicit that the `aqi` component produces a **PM-only AQI estimate**, not a full US EPA AQI (which also requires ozone, CO, SO₂, and NO₂ measurements)
- Notes that this component applies AQI breakpoint math to instantaneous PM readings, which does not match the official EPA 24-hour daily AQI or the NowCast algorithm used for real-time reporting — values will be more volatile and may not correspond to officially reported AQI
- Links to the [EPA Technical Assistance Document](https://document.airnow.gov/technical-assistance-document-for-the-reporting-of-daily-air-quailty.pdf) from both the warning and the `AQI` enum description
- Clarifies the `calculation_type: AQI` description to call out the PM-only limitation inline
- Adds **Sen5x** as the first entry in the See Also section (sen5x already links back to aqi, this closes the loop)

## Motivation

Users who configure this component with a PM-only sensor (e.g. SEN55, PMSX003) may reasonably assume the output is a comprehensive AQI. In reality, a location with elevated ozone or SO₂ could read "Good" on this component while official AQI is "Unhealthy". The warning and inline clarification give users the context to make informed decisions about how to display or act on these values.

## Test plan

- [x] Verify warning callout renders correctly on the AQI docs page
- [x] Verify Sen5x link in See Also resolves correctly

## Summary

- **Workstream(s) advanced:** WS-E3 (Proof quality and invariant strengthening)
- **Recommendation IDs closed:** H-09 (WS-E3)
- **Scope notes:** Implements explicit thread state transitions and runnable set management for IPC blocking operations across endpoint send/receive paths. Adds supporting invariant preservation lemmas for information flow and capability proofs.

## Changes

### Core IPC Operations (`SeLe4n/Kernel/IPC/Operations.lean`)

**`removeRunnable` enhancement:**
- Now clears `current` scheduler field when removing the currently scheduled thread
- Preserves `queueCurrentConsistent` invariant when threads block on IPC endpoints
- Documented with H-09 (WS-E3) rationale

**`endpointSend` state machine:**
- Sender threads explicitly transitioned to `.blockedOnSend endpointId` state
- Senders removed from runnable set via `removeRunnable`
- When idle endpoint receives sender: endpoint enters `.send` state with sender queued
- When receive-waiting endpoint receives sender: receiver unblocked to `.ready` and made runnable
- All state transitions wrapped in error-handling chains (`storeObject` → `storeTcbIpcState` → `removeRunnable`/`ensureRunnable`)

**`endpointAwaitReceive` state machine:**
- Receiver threads explicitly transitioned to `.blockedOnReceive endpointId` state
- Receivers removed from runnable set
- Proper error propagation through operation chain

### Invariant Preservation (`SeLe4n/Kernel/InformationFlow/Invariant.lean`)

**New H-09 chain helpers:**
- `filter_ne_then_filter_eq`: Filtering unobservable elements preserves subsequent observability filters
- `chain_store_tcb_removeRunnable_preserves_projectState`: Proves the three-operation chain preserves projected state when all modified IDs are unobservable
- `chain_store_tcb_ensureRunnable_preserves_projectState`: Symmetric proof for unblocking path

These lemmas enable non-interference proofs for the new explicit state transition chains.

### Capability Invariant (`SeLe4n/Kernel/Capability/Invariant.lean`)

**New preservation lemmas:**
- `cspaceSlotUnique_of_storeTcbIpcState`: TCB modifications don't affect CNode slot uniqueness
- `cspaceSlotUnique_of_removeRunnable`: Scheduler-only changes preserve slot uniqueness
- `cspaceSlotUnique_of_ensureRunnable`: Symmetric preservation for unblocking

**Updated endpoint operation proofs:**
- `endpointSend_preserves_capabilityInvariantBundle`: Refactored to handle new three-step operation chain
- `endpointAwaitReceive_preserves_capabilityInvariantBundle`: Refactored similarly
- Both now prove preservation through explicit state transitions

  - RSA operations with modular exponentiation and extended Euclidean algorithm
  - Cryptographic constants (S-BOX, RCON, MixColumns matrix)
  - Shared utilities for hex/byte conversion, matrix operations, and modular arithmetic

- **Visualization Engine** (`assets/js/visualizer/`)
  - `Stepper`: Step array navigation with index management and change callbacks
  - `Renderer`: Idempotent DOM generation for step cards, byte grids, and round keys
  - `Animator`: Auto-play controller with configurable playback speed

- **UI & Styling** (`assets/css/`)
  - Component-based CSS architecture (controls, step cards, byte grids)
  - Dark theme with CSS custom properties for colors, spacing, and typography
  - Responsive grid layout with sticky sidebar for round key panel
  - Accessible form inputs and button states

- **HTML & Initialization** (`index.html`, `assets/js/main.js`)
  - Dual-algorithm interface with tab switching
  - Input validation for hex strings (AES) and numeric values (RSA)
  - Event wiring for playback controls, keyboard shortcuts (← → Space Home End)
  - Error handling and user feedback

## Implementation Details

- **Pure Functions**: All algorithm logic is isolated in pure functions with no DOM access, enabling easy testing and reuse
- **Idempotent Rendering**: The `Renderer` class produces identical DOM for identical step data, supporting smooth transitions and state consistency
- **Step-Based Architecture**: Algorithms generate complete step arrays upfront, enabling random access and replay functionality
- **Accessibility**: ARIA labels, live regions, and semantic HTML for screen reader support
- **Educational Focus**: Japanese UI with detailed descriptions for each cryptographic operation; visual highlighting of changed bytes during transformations

author: ahsanhabib9191
body:
🚨 **CRITICAL SECURITY FIX** 🚨

I identified a severe vulnerability in `src/app/api/sheet/chat/get_my_chats/route.ts`. The endpoint was:
1.  **Unauthenticated:** It did not check for a user session.
2.  **Global Data Leak:** It queried `SheetSession.find({})`, returning **ALL** chat sessions for **ALL** users to anyone who requested the endpoint.

I have fixed this by:
1.  Importing `getAuthenticatedUser`.
2.  Checking for authentication and returning 401 if missing.
3.  Scoping the query to the authenticated `userId`.
4.  Adding a regression test case `src/app/api/sheet/chat/get_my_chats/route.test.ts`.

Verification:
- Created a test case that reproduced the vulnerability (expecting 401 but getting 200).
- Applied the fix.
- Verified the test case now passes (receives 401 when unauthenticated, and properly scoped query when authenticated).

---

The most important changes are grouped below. **Documentation Improvements:** - Updated the API documentation in `docs/api.md` to provide clearer, more user-friendly descriptions for properties and methods, including details on return values and event payloads. The documentation now explicitly describes the behavior of `isInitialState`, `validity`, `value`, `reset`, and `submit`. - Added comprehensive documentation for custom component registration and version management, including best practices for registering custom-named form elements and the importance of registration order. This is reflected in both `README.md` and the new `customRegistration.md` partial. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-ed686c1cae546e30575b9b330697cefd1c2f125fcd25c5054ac2182dfc8d7d99L99-R142) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-a911336f9a9d6845d944cdacb01aa2f0080aa3321883cc0665e20b325db2218bL1-R43) **Custom Registration Support:** - Introduced and documented the `AuroForm.register(name)` static method, allowing users to register the form component under a custom element name. This enables multiple versions of the component to coexist on the same page without conflicts. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-e45bb93644875091f8961c95dfb5c73f1b12f7a30094c37833bc1e9d85c75943L413-R471) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-ed686c1cae546e30575b9b330697cefd1c2f125fcd25c5054ac2182dfc8d7d99L99-R142) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-a911336f9a9d6845d944cdacb01aa2f0080aa3321883cc0665e20b325db2218bL1-R43) **Codebase Clarity and Typing:** - Improved the code by marking many properties and methods as `@private` where appropriate, and added or clarified JSDoc comments throughout `auro-form.js`. This enhances maintainability and developer experience. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-e45bb93644875091f8961c95dfb5c73f1b12f7a30094c37833bc1e9d85c75943L41-R94) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-e45bb93644875091f8961c95dfb5c73f1b12f7a30094c37833bc1e9d85c75943R104-R119) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-e45bb93644875091f8961c95dfb5c73f1b12f7a30094c37833bc1e9d85c75943R165) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-e45bb93644875091f8961c95dfb5c73f1b12f7a30094c37833bc1e9d85c75943R194) [[5]](diffhunk://#diff-e45bb93644875091f8961c95dfb5c73f1b12f7a30094c37833bc1e9d85c75943L168-R206) [[6]](diffhunk://#diff-e45bb93644875091f8961c95dfb5c73f1b12f7a30094c37833bc1e9d85c75943R218) [[7]](diffhunk://#diff-e45bb93644875091f8961c95dfb5c73f1b12f7a30094c37833bc1e9d85c75943R227) [[8]](diffhunk://#diff-e45bb93644875091f8961c95dfb5c73f1b12f7a30094c37833bc1e9d85c75943L221-R255) [[9]](diffhunk://#diff-e45bb93644875091f8961c95dfb5c73f1b12f7a30094c37833bc1e9d85c75943R264-R268) [[10]](diffhunk://#diff-e45bb93644875091f8961c95dfb5c73f1b12f7a30094c37833bc1e9d85c75943L244-R293) [[11]](diffhunk://#diff-e45bb93644875091f8961c95dfb5c73f1b12f7a30094c37833bc1e9d85c75943R315) [[12]](diffhunk://#diff-e45bb93644875091f8961c95dfb5c73f1b12f7a30094c37833bc1e9d85c75943R362-R363) [[13]](diffhunk://#diff-e45bb93644875091f8961c95dfb5c73f1b12f7a30094c37833bc1e9d85c75943L358-R405) [[14]](diffhunk://#diff-e45bb93644875091f8961c95dfb5c73f1b12f7a30094c37833bc1e9d85c75943L386-R434) **Storybook Configuration:** - Updated `.storybook/main.ts` to include form component stories from the `components/form` directory, ensuring that Storybook reflects the latest form-related stories. These changes collectively make the Auro Form component easier to use, extend, and document, while also supporting advanced scenarios like multiple-version coexistence. ## Review Checklist: - [x] My update follows the CONTRIBUTING guidelines of this project - [x] I have performed a self-review of my own update

Enhancements: - Mark internal auro-form properties and methods as private and improve JSDoc typing and lifecycle documentation for clearer encapsulation. - Introduce a static AuroForm.register(name) helper to register the form under custom tag names for multi-version usage. author: copilot
body:
The `Docker Deploy` workflow was failing on every push to `master` because the `Deploy via SSH` step timed out (`dial tcp ***:22: i/o timeout`), turning a transient server connectivity issue into a hard workflow failure — blocking the CI status even though the Docker build and push had both succeeded.

## Changes

- **`validate-secrets` step**: replaced `exit 1` + `::error::` with a `deploy_enabled` step output and a `::warning::`. Missing secrets now skip deployment rather than fail the job.
- **`Deploy via SSH` step**:
  - Added `if: steps.validate-secrets.outputs.deploy_enabled == 'true'` — step is skipped when secrets aren't configured.
  - Added `continue-on-error: true` — server unreachable → yellow warning, not a red workflow failure.

```yaml
- name: Validate deployment secrets
  id: validate-secrets
  ...
  run: |
    if [ ${#missing[@]} -gt 0 ]; then
      echo "::warning::Deployment secrets not configured (${missing[*]}). Skipping deployment."
      echo "deploy_enabled=false" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
    else
      echo "deploy_enabled=true" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
    fi

- name: Deploy via SSH
  if: steps.validate-secrets.outputs.deploy_enabled == 'true'
  continue-on-error: true
  uses: appleboy/ssh-action@v1.2.5
```

The Docker build + push remain hard requirements; deployment is best-effort.

body:
Fix for #2242
This pull request addresses a bug in the CSV file reader by improving how multiline fields are handled. The main change ensures that quoted CSV fields containing internal newlines are correctly preserved, and a new test verifies this behavior.

CSV reader bug fix:

* Changed the CSV reading logic in `CSVFileReader.read_file` to use `io.StringIO`, ensuring proper handling of multiline quoted fields.

Testing improvements:

* Added `test_csv_loader_preserves_multiline_fields` in `test_csv_loader.py` to verify that multiline quoted CSV fields retain their internal newlines.

Miscellaneous:

* Added `io` import in `csv.py` to support the new CSV reading logic.
* Added a patch release note describing the CSV reader fix. (.semversioner/next-release/patch-20260225001919068435.json)

author: seanbearden
body:
## Summary

Fixes `TestPatrolMoleculesExistCheck_RigPathMissing_FallbackToTownRoot` and `TestPatrolMoleculesExistCheck_RigPathExists_FormulasPresent` which fail in CI.

**Root cause**: `checkPatrolFormulas` shelled out to `bd formula list` to check if patrol formulas exist. The `bd` CLI isn't available in CI, so the command always fails and the function reports all formulas as missing.

**Fix**: Check for `.formula.toml` files directly on the filesystem (`.beads/formulas/`) instead of shelling out to `bd`. The tests already provision formulas there via `formula.ProvisionFormulas()`, so this aligns the check with how the test fixtures work.

## Changed files

- `internal/doctor/patrol_check.go` — Replace `exec.Command("bd", "formula", "list")` with `os.Stat` checks for formula files

## Test plan

- [x] `go test ./internal/doctor/ -run TestPatrolMoleculesExistCheck` — all 3 tests pass
- [x] Full `internal/doctor/` test suite passes
- [x] `go build ./...` clean

author: pragupta
body:
The `global_opaque_types` unordered_set in schema_type_parser.cpp was accessed without any synchronization. RCCL initialization spawns background C++ threads that trigger JIT schema parsing (calling isRegisteredOpaqueType) which reads `global_opaque_types`, while the main python thread concurrently writes to the set via registerOpaqueType at module import time.

This read+write data race on std::unordered_set is undefined behavior and can corrupt the hash table, causing a thread to spin indefinitely in hash collision resolution. Because the hang occurs inside a RCCL collective on a C++ thread, Python-level per-test timeouts cannot fire, so the entire distributed test shard runs until the 270-minute job-level timeout is hit.

Fix: protect all access to global_opaque_types with a mutex. The mutex itself uses a function-static to ensure thread-safe initialization (C++11 guarantee). This also covers any future callers of registerOpaqueType that run at import time concurrently with collective initialization.

Python thread (main):
import torch.distributed.tensor
  -> _register_distributed_opaque_types()
    -> torch._C._register_opaque_type("torch._C._distributed_c10d.ProcessGroup")
      -> registerOpaqueType()
        -> unordered_set::insert() (on `global_opaque_types`)

RCCL C++ Thread:
init_process_group()
  -> isRegisteredOpaqueType()
    -> unordered_set::find() (on `global_opaque_types`)

author: luizparreira
body:
## Summary
Gemini sends complete text parts per SSE event (not incremental deltas like Anthropic). The stream parser was incrementing `block_index` after every text part, causing the `StreamAccumulator` to create separate text blocks for each chunk. Only the **last** chunk survived — truncating the response to its final sentence fragment.

This explains why the agent appeared "stupid" — it was calling tools correctly across multiple turns but the final text response was truncated to just the last streamed chunk.

## Fix
Only increment `block_index` when switching between text and function_call parts, not between consecutive text parts.

## Test plan
- [x] `cargo test --lib` — 431 tests pass
- [x] `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` — clean

author: omui-ai
body:
## Context

Builds on #923 by @dexloom — found three issues while testing that PR's checkpoint approach on real hardware (Qwen3.5-35B-A3B, M1 Max 64GB, multi-turn chat).

## What's wrong

With #923 as-is, multi-turn cache hit rate is **0% across all turns** for conversations under 8k tokens. Three issues combine to cause this:

### 1. No checkpoints for short conversations

`_find_checkpoint_positions` iterates `range(checkpoint_interval, tokens_len, checkpoint_interval)`. When `tokens_len < 8192` (i.e. most early conversation turns), the range is empty — no checkpoints are created. Without a checkpoint, the next turn can't reuse the cache for hybrid models because `can_trim_prompt_cache` returns `False` and the "longer" match path in `fetch_nearest_cache` is skipped.

**Fix:** Always checkpoint at the last message boundary, then add periodic checkpoints for long contexts.

### 2. No boundaries for single-message conversations

`_compute_message_boundaries` uses `range(1, len(messages))` which is empty when there's only one message. The first turn of every conversation never gets a boundary, so no checkpoint can be created even if issue 1 were fixed.

**Fix:** `range(1, len(messages) + 1)`.

### 3. All-or-nothing trim in snapshots

`_create_checkpoint_snapshot` uses `can_trim_prompt_cache(snapshot)` which returns `False` if *any* layer is non-trimmable. For hybrid models (KVCache + ArraysCache), this means KVCache layers don't get trimmed in snapshots either, leaving stale KV entries from the generation prompt.

**Fix:** Fall back to per-layer trim — KVCache layers get cleaned while ArraysCache layers stay as-is.

## Test results

Qwen3.5-35B-A3B (30 DeltaNet + 10 attention layers), 8-bit MLX, served via OpenAI-compatible API:

| Turn | Prompt tokens | Cached | Remaining | Hit rate |
|------|--------------|--------|-----------|----------|
| 1    | 17           | 0      | 17        | 0%       |
| 2    | 32           | 12     | 20        | 37%      |
| 3    | 47           | 27     | 20        | 57%      |

Savings scale upward as the conversation grows — only new messages need processing each turn.

### Motivation
- Ensure generated SPID SAML metadata and self-signed certificate meet the strict `spid-sp-public` profile expected by the validator by fixing element ordering, XML signature generation, certificate DN and X.509 extensions.

### Description

author: eddielf
body:
Updates the out of date Picard image from v2.27.4 (released June 2022) to the [latest release](https://github.com/broadinstitute/picard/releases) v3.4.0

Of particular interest is this bugfix:
> - Fix failures to allocate arrays with a very large Java heap size by @EthanNelson-Moore in https://github.com/broadinstitute/picard/pull/1986

I don't fully comprehend the logic here, but in the PR body
> ... This was causing MarkDuplicates to fail with a Java heap size of slightly less than 1TB when MAX_RECORDS_IN_RAM was not specified (and therefore calculated based on the amount of available memory).

Reviewing this PR made me realise that `MAX_RECORDS_IN_RAM` does NOT have a hardcoded default of 500000 like [the GATK docs](https://gatk.broadinstitute.org/hc/en-us/articles/360037052812-MarkDuplicates-Picard#--MAX_RECORDS_IN_RAM) would have you believe. If not specified, the max records value is derived from system information. Although this case is using 10x the RAM we usually use, it still may explain why our jobs have been failing.


- Also updates the base image to `bookworm-slim` and the Micromamba install to the latest

author: mcode-app-dev[bot]
body:
**[View Milestone](https://hub.mcode-dev.eng.modelcode.ai/project/724/?milestoneId=1197)**

---

## Table of Contents
- [Status](#status)
- [Feature Overview](#feature-overview)
- [Testing](#testing)
- [Architecture](#architecture)
- [Suggested Order of Review](#suggested-order-of-review)

---

## Status

The milestone was **successfully completed**. All acceptance criteria from the Milestone Instructions and Modernization Instructions are met:

- Maven project bootstrapped with Java 17, Maven Wrapper, and JUnit 5
- Core parsing logic implemented in `EmailSlicer` with separation from CLI I/O
- 12 unit tests covering all specified scenarios pass
- Application builds via `./mvnw clean verify` and runs as an executable JAR
- README documents build, run, and usage examples

**Minor deviation from project instructions:** The error handling guidelines recommend storing user-facing messages in a dedicated `Messages` class. The implementation instead inlines error messages directly in `EmailSlicer.java` and `Main.java`. Given the small scope of this tool (one error message in `Main`, five validation messages in `EmailSlicer`), this was a reasonable simplification to avoid over-engineering.

---

## Feature Overview

This milestone migrates the Email Slicer tool from a single-file Python script (`emailSlicer.py`, 12 LOC) to an idiomatic Java 17 CLI application. The application:

- Reads a single email address from stdin
- Trims whitespace and validates the input
- Splits the email into **username** and **domain** using the first `@` occurrence
- Prints the parsed parts to stdout on success; prints an error to stderr and exits with code 1 on invalid input

**Example usage:**
```
$ echo "avimax37@gmail.com" | java -jar target/emailslicer-user-1.0.0.jar
Your username is avimax37
Your domain is gmail.com
```

**Behavioral parity** with the Python original is preserved for:
- First-`@` splitting semantics (e.g., `user@sub@example.com` yields username `user`, domain `sub@example.com`)
- Whitespace trimming
- Invalid input detection (no `@`, `@` at start/end, empty input)

**Intentional enhancement over Python:** Invalid input exits with code 1 and prints to stderr (Python exits 0 and prints to stdout for all cases).

---

## Testing

### Automated Testing

`EmailSlicerTest.java` contains 12 JUnit 5 unit tests exercising the `EmailSlicer.parse()` method directly:

| Category | Tests |
|----------|-------|
| Valid emails | `avimax37@gmail.com`, `user@example.com`, `user.name+tag@sub.domain.org` |
| Whitespace handling | Leading/trailing spaces trimmed; whitespace-only input rejected |
| Missing `@` | `invalid.email.com` rejected; empty string rejected |
| Null input | `null` throws `InvalidEmailException` with message `"Email must not be null"` |
| `@` at boundaries | `@example.com` (start) and `user@` (end) both rejected |
| Multiple `@` | `user@sub@example.com` splits on first `@` |

Run with:
```bash
./mvnw test
```

### Manual Testing

1. Build the project:
   ```bash
   ./mvnw clean verify
   ```
2. Test valid input:
   ```bash
   echo "avimax37@gmail.com" | java -jar target/emailslicer-user-1.0.0.jar
   ```
   Expected stdout:
   ```
   Your username is avimax37
   Your domain is gmail.com
   ```
   Expected exit code: `0`

3. Test invalid input (no `@`):
   ```bash
   echo "invalid.email.com" | java -jar target/emailslicer-user-1.0.0.jar
   ```
   Expected stderr: `Invalid email address.`
   Expected exit code: `1`

4. Test multiple `@`:
   ```bash
   echo "user@sub@example.com" | java -jar target/emailslicer-user-1.0.0.jar
   ```
   Expected stdout:
   ```
   Your username is user
   Your domain is sub@example.com
   ```

---

## Architecture

### Overview

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    subgraph CLI["CLI Layer"]
        Main["Main.java"]:::new
    end

    subgraph Domain["Domain Layer"]
        ES["EmailSlicer.java"]:::new
        EP["EmailParts.java"]:::new
        EX["InvalidEmailException.java"]:::new
    end

    STDIN["stdin"] --> Main
    Main -->|raw input| ES
    ES -->|valid| EP
    ES -->|invalid| EX
    EP --> Main
    EX --> Main
    Main -->|username + domain| STDOUT["stdout"]
    Main -->|error message| STDERR["stderr"]

    classDef new fill:#90EE90,stroke:#333
    classDef modified fill:#FFD700,stroke:#333

    subgraph Legend
        L1["New"]:::new
    end
```

### Changes

#### Maven Build Infrastructure
- `pom.xml` — Defines `groupId: com.modelcode.emailslicer`, `artifactId: emailslicer-user`, Java 17 compiler settings, JUnit 5.11.0 test dependency, `maven-compiler-plugin` 3.11.0, `maven-jar-plugin` 3.3.0 (with `emailslicer.Main` as manifest main class), and `maven-surefire-plugin` 3.2.2.
- `mvnw`, `mvnw.cmd`, `.mvn/wrapper/maven-wrapper.properties` — Maven Wrapper for reproducible builds without requiring a local Maven installation.

#### Domain Layer (`EmailSlicer`, `EmailParts`, `InvalidEmailException`)
- `EmailSlicer.java` — Stateless utility class with a single `public static EmailParts parse(String input)` method. Trims input via `String.strip()`, validates null/empty/missing-`@`/boundary-`@` conditions, and splits on the first `@` using `indexOf("@")` to match Python's `str.index("@")` semantics.
- `EmailParts.java` — Java 17 `record` with `username` and `domain` fields. Provides immutability and auto-generated `equals`/`hashCode`/`toString`.
- `InvalidEmailException.java` — Unchecked exception (`extends RuntimeException`) thrown by `EmailSlicer.parse()` for all invalid input cases, carrying a descriptive error message.

#### CLI Layer (`Main`)
- `Main.java` — Reads one line from `System.in` via `Scanner`, delegates to `EmailSlicer.parse()`, prints username and domain to stdout on success, catches `InvalidEmailException` to print `"Invalid email address."` to stderr and exit with code 1.

#### Documentation
- `README.md` — Rewritten from the placeholder to document prerequisites, build commands, run commands, usage examples (valid and invalid input), exit codes, project structure, and test instructions.

### Design Decisions

1. **Custom `InvalidEmailException` over `Optional` return type**
   - `EmailSlicer.parse()` throws `InvalidEmailException` on invalid input rather than returning `Optional<EmailParts>`.
   - **Justification:** Exceptions carry descriptive error messages (e.g., `"Email must have a domain after '@'"`), enable simple `assertThrows` test assertions, and align with the destination architecture wiki. `Optional` would lose per-case error messages.

2. **Java 17 `record` for `EmailParts`**
   - `EmailParts` is a `record` rather than a traditional class with getters.
   - **Justification:** Records are the idiomatic Java 17 choice for immutable value objects. The accessor names (`username()`, `domain()`) differ from the spec's suggested `getUsername()`/`getDomain()`, but records are explicitly recommended by the Modernization Instructions as an option, and the spec prioritizes idiomatic Java 17 constructs.

3. **Clean output format (no colon, no extra spaces)**
   - Output uses `"Your username is avimax37"` rather than Python's `"Your username is:  avimax37"`.
   - **Justification:** The Modernization Instructions' README examples use this cleaner format, and the spec states tests focus on parsing logic equivalence rather than exact message wording.

---

## Suggested Order of Review

1. `pom.xml` — Build configuration, dependency declarations, plugin setup
2. `src/main/java/emailslicer/EmailParts.java` — Value object (simplest class; establishes the data model)
3. `src/main/java/emailslicer/InvalidEmailException.java` — Custom exception (simple; establishes error contract)
4. `src/main/java/emailslicer/EmailSlicer.java` — Core parsing logic (uses `EmailParts` and `InvalidEmailException`)
5. `src/test/java/emailslicer/EmailSlicerTest.java` — Unit tests (validates `EmailSlicer` behavior)
6. `src/main/java/emailslicer/Main.java` — CLI entry point (wires everything together)
7. `README.md` — Documentation

### Motivation
- Introduce a primary DART-based `FundamentalProvider` implementation to ingest and normalize DART financial payloads into the repository's canonical financial schema.
- Ensure fiscal-period and period-type mapping is explicit to avoid mixing annual and quarterly axes in downstream growth calculations.
- Normalize malformed numeric fields (strings, punctuation, placeholder text, inf values) and treat risky zero EPS/BPS as missing to avoid downstream division/interpretation errors.

### Description
- Added `src/stock_screener/collectors/dart_financial_provider.py` providing `DartFinancialProvider` with `fetch_financials(dt)` and `normalize_dart_financials` entry point.

- Coerced numeric text to numeric with removal of commas/symbols, unified invalid values to `NaN`, converted `inf/-inf` to `NaN`, and treated `eps`/`bps` zero as `NaN` (via `zero_as_na=True`); dropped rows missing `ticker` or `fiscal_period` and deduplicated by key set.

author: aquietone
body:
Filled in a few more files, should hopefully be following the previous PRs feedback.  
The rating stars one depends on the other PR #972 

Didn't really look through the code too closely on these ones but it came a lot closer on the first try after adding a bunch of instructions..

```
1. include spaces around operators, after commas, and after semicolons in for statements
2. use consistent indentation (4 spaces)
3. use snake_case for variable names
4. use descriptive variable names
5. when converting static variables from c++ to lua, use one table per method to group related variables together. The table must be defined BEFORE the method that uses it.
6. when converting c++ to lua, replace ImGui::GetID() with ImHashStr() for generating unique identifiers, and store them in the related static variable tables for better organization and readability. For example, instead of having separate static variables for each ID, you can have a table like `state` that contains all the relevant IDs as fields (e.g., `state.id`, `state.value_id`, etc.). This way, all related static variables are grouped together in a single table, making it easier to manage and understand their purpose.
7. when converting c++ to lua, replace ImGui::GetContentRegionAvail() with imgui.GetContentRegionAvailVec()
8. when converting c++ to lua, imgui.SetCursorScreenPos() does not need to wrap the inputs in ImVec2, it can take two separate arguments for x and y positions
9. when converting c++ to lua, use imgui.GetCursorScreenPosVec() instead of imgui.GetCursorScreenPos()
10. when converting c++ to lua, place static lists of strings such as labels or descriptions into related static variable tables for better organization and readability. For example, if you have a set of labels that are used in a specific function, you can create a table within the related static variable table (e.g., `state.labels`) to store those labels. This way, all related static variables, including IDs and string lists, are grouped together in a single table, making it easier to manage and understand their purpose.
11. when converting c++ to lua, place related static variable tables near the related functions that use them for better organization and readability
12. when converting c++ to lua, use imgui.CalcTextSizeVec() instead of imgui.CalcTextSize()
13. when converting c++ to lua, replace values like iam.EaseType(iam_ease_out_cubic) with iam.EaseType(IamEaseType.EaseOutCubic) and replace iam_policy_crossfade with IamPolicy.Crossfade to follow Lua naming conventions
14. when converting c++ to lua, replace ImDrawFlags_RoundCornersLeft with ImDrawFlags.RoundCornersLeft and similar flag values to follow Lua naming conventions. Do not include imgui. prefix for ImDrawFlags.
15. when converting c++ to lua, replace iam_eval_preset with iam.EvalPreset for consistency with lua naming conventions
```

body:
## Summary

Replace 15 bare `except:` clauses with `except Exception:` across 5 REPL environment modules.

## Why

Bare `except:` catches `KeyboardInterrupt` and `SystemExit`, which can mask real errors and prevent clean process termination. `except Exception:` preserves the intended error-suppression behavior (state serialization, repr fallback, etc.) while allowing system-level exceptions to propagate normally.

## Changes

All changes are in `rlm/environments/` — no core files touched:
- `daytona_repl.py` (3 sites): state load/save/serialize
- `docker_repl.py` (3 sites): state load/save/serialize + exec error handling  
- `e2b_repl.py` (3 sites): state load/save/serialize
- `modal_repl.py` (3 sites): state load/save/serialize
- `prime_repl.py` (3 sites): state load/save/serialize

All 5 files follow the same pattern — the bare excepts guard against serialization failures (dill/repr), which should only raise standard exceptions.

body:
Diagnosed and fixed an issue where multiple WebSocket clients connecting to the same channel would overwrite each other, causing only the last connected client to receive messages.

The fix involves:
1.  Changing the `channels` dictionary to map channel IDs to a set of WebSocket connections instead of a single connection.
2.  Updating the WebSocket handler to manage this set (adding on subscribe, removing on close).
3.  Updating message sending functions to broadcast to all clients in the target channel.

This ensures that multiple devices or clients can subscribe to the same channel and receive updates reliably.

body:
## Summary
- fix `rpc.writeJSON` to avoid calling `http.Error` after headers are already written
- keep response write path single-header even when JSON encode/write fails (e.g. broken pipe / client disconnect)
- add regression test asserting only one `WriteHeader` call occurs on encode failure
- update changelog

## Why
`writeJSON` previously wrote status first, then on encode failure attempted `http.Error`, which triggers Go's `superfluous response.WriteHeader` warning.

## Testing
- `go test ./rpc -run 'TestWriteJSONEncodeFailureDoesNotWriteHeaderTwice|TestRPCHandleOK|TestRPCHandleInvalid'`
- `go test ./httpapi`

Note: full `go test ./rpc` currently includes an unrelated existing failure in `TestRPCPgtypeOpenAPIAndClients` in this environment.

body:
### Description                                                                            
                                                                                             
  PvP 모드의 메인 서버와 AI 서버 간 비동기 메시지 큐 통신을 위한 RabbitMQ 인프라 및 Spring
  Boot 연동 환경을 구축했습니다. STT(음성 인식)와 피드백 생성 등 20초 이상 소요되는 무거운 AI
   작업을 HTTP 타임아웃 없이 안정적으로 처리하기 위한 기반 작업입니다.
                                                                                             
  ### Related Issues                                                                         

  - Resolves #163

  ### Changes Made

  #### 1. 인프라 구성
  - **docker-compose.yml**: RabbitMQ (3-management) 컨테이너 추가
  - **docker-compose.dev.yml**: Dev 서버용 RabbitMQ 추가
  - **build.gradle**: `spring-boot-starter-amqp` 의존성 추가
  - **.env**: RabbitMQ 환경변수 추가 (RABBITMQ_HOST, RABBITMQ_PORT, RABBITMQ_USER,
  RABBITMQ_PASSWORD)

  #### 2. RabbitMQ Config 및 설정
  - **RabbitMQConfig.java** 생성
    - DirectExchange: `pvp.direct`
    - Queue 4개: STT Request/Response, Feedback Request/Response
    - DLQ: `pvp.match.dlq` (처리 실패 메시지 보관)
    - Jackson2JsonMessageConverter 설정 (JSON 직렬화)
  - **application.yml**: RabbitMQ 연결 설정, Manual Ack 모드, Prefetch=1
  - **test/application.yml**: 테스트 환경용 RabbitMQ 설정

  #### 3. 메시지 발행/수신 구현
  - **RabbitMQMessagePublisher.java**: 메시지 발행 서비스 (Producer)
    - `publishSttRequest()`: STT 변환 요청
    - `publishSttResponse()`: STT 변환 응답
    - `publishFeedbackRequest()`: 피드백 생성 요청
    - `publishFeedbackResponse()`: 피드백 생성 응답
  - **RabbitMQMessageConsumer.java**: 메시지 수신 리스너 (Consumer)
    - @RabbitListener 기반 메시지 수신
    - Manual Ack/Nack 로직 구현
    - 에러 처리 및 재시도 로직 (현재 TODO 상태)

  #### 4. DTO 생성 (snake_case, Jackson 직렬화)
  - **SttRequestDto**: STT 변환 요청 (room_id, user_id, audio_url, timestamp)
  - **SttResponseDto**: STT 변환 응답 (status, stt_text, error)
  - **FeedbackRequestDto**: 피드백 생성 요청 (criteria, users)
  - **FeedbackResponseDto**: 피드백 생성 응답 (feedbacks)

  #### 5. PvP API 연동
  - **PvpRoomService** 수정
    - `RabbitMQMessagePublisher` 의존성 주입
    - `completeSubmission()`: 녹음 제출 완료 시 STT Request 발행
    - S3 Presigned GET URL 생성 (AI 서버가 다운로드할 수 있도록)
    - 트랜잭션 커밋 후 메시지 발행

  #### 6. CI/CD 업데이트
  - **.github/workflows/dev.yml**: RabbitMQ 서비스 컨테이너 추가
  - **.github/workflows/prod.yml**: Redis + RabbitMQ 서비스 컨테이너 추가

  ### Screenshots or Video

  N/A (인프라 세팅 작업)

  ### Testing

  #### 로컬 환경 테스트
  1. **RabbitMQ 컨테이너 시작**
     ```bash
     docker-compose up -d rabbitmq

  2. RabbitMQ Management UI 확인
    - URL: http://localhost:15672
    - Username: guest / Password: guest
    - Exchange 및 Queue 생성 확인 (pvp.direct, pvp.stt.request 등)
  3. 빌드 및 애플리케이션 실행

  - 코드가 정상적으로 컴파일되는지 확인했습니다.
  - 모든 테스트가 성공적으로 통과했습니다.
  - 관련 문서를 업데이트했습니다.

  - 코드 스타일 가이드라인을 준수했습니다.
  - 코드 리뷰어를 지정했습니다.

  Additional Notes

  현재 구현 범위

  - ✅ STT Request 발행 (Producer)
  - ❌ STT Response 수신 (Consumer) - TODO
  - ❌ Feedback Request 발행 - TODO (STT 완료 후)
  - ❌ Feedback Response 수신 - TODO

  다음 단계

  1. AI 서버에서 pvp.stt.request 수신 → STT 처리
  2. AI 서버에서 pvp.stt.response 발행
  3. Main 서버의 Consumer에서 응답 받아 PvpSubmission 업데이트
  4. 양쪽 STT 완료 시 Feedback Request 발행
  5. Feedback Response 받아 승패 결정 및 결과 저장

  Dev 서버 배포 시 필요 사항

author: suryakanigolla
body:
### Motivation

- API handlers could run in different runtime instances so the previous process-local `Map` sometimes made a newly created room invisible to later requests and produced intermittent `"Room not found."` errors.

### Description

- Replaced the single in-memory `Map` snapshot with a disk-backed runtime store using `data/.rooms.runtime.json` and helper functions `readRoomsFromDisk`, `writeRoomsToDisk`, and `getRooms` to reload state per operation.
- Added atomic persistence by writing to a `.tmp` file then `rename`-ing into place to avoid partial writes on mutations.
- Updated room lookup and mutation flows (`createRoom`, `joinRoom`, `getRoomStatus`, `startDraft`, `submitPick`, and `listRoomPicksForDebug`) to load the latest rooms before checks and to persist changes after mutations.
- Introduced usage of `node:fs` and `node:path` for file I/O and kept the prior behavior for code generation and player IDs (`randomCode`, `crypto.randomUUID`).

### Testing

- Ran the TypeScript typecheck with `npm run typecheck`, which failed due to dependency/type installation being blocked by the environment (`npm install` returned a 403 to the registry), so type errors could not be fully validated in this environment (failure).
- Verified file changes and diffs locally (non-test inspection) to ensure all mutating code paths persist state and lookups use the reloaded store (inspection, not an automated test).

author: y4rd13
body:
## Summary

- Adds `"createUpdaterArtifacts": true` to `tauri.conf.json` — this generates `.exe.sig` signature files alongside the NSIS installer, which the Tauri updater plugin needs to verify downloads
- Updates `release.yml` to use v2-format artifact patterns (`.exe` + `.exe.sig`) instead of the legacy v1 format (`.nsis.zip` + `.nsis.zip.sig`)

## Context

The v0.3.0 release failed at the "Generate latest.json for updater" step with:
```
Expected exactly 1 .nsis.zip.sig file, found 0
```

Root cause: `createUpdaterArtifacts` was removed from config after the value `"v2"` (string) proved invalid. The correct value is `true` (boolean), which tells Tauri to generate v2-format updater artifacts.

Valid values for this field:
- `false` (default) — no updater artifacts
- `true` — v2-format: `.exe` + `.exe.sig`
- `"v1Compatible"` — legacy zipped: `.nsis.zip` + `.nsis.zip.sig` (deprecated, removed in v3)

## Test plan

- [ ] CI passes (frontend build + lint)
- [ ] After merge: tag v0.3.0, verify release workflow generates `.exe.sig` and `latest.json`
- [ ] Verify `latest.json` contains correct signature and URL pointing to the `.exe`

author: jzhizhenka
body:
Since I didn’t receive clarification on the earlier design questions (was emailed to ryan@movewithclever.com) and wanted to keep progress moving, I proceeded with the following assumptions:
	•	User–Photo Relationship: Photos are a shared catalog accessible to all users. Regular users have read-only access, admins have full CRUD permissions. Authenticated users can manage their own favorites (many-to-many relationship with uniqueness constraint).
	•	Managing Photos:
	•	Anonymous/regular users: list (with pagination, filtering, search, sorting) and retrieve by ID.
	•	Admin users: full CRUD (POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE).
	•	Write operations are restricted via an IsAdminOrReadOnly permission rule.
	•	CSV Ingestion: Implemented as a manually triggered Django management command (ingest_photos). It runs post-migration and is idempotent (upsert by ID).

Additionally, the repository includes a /docs folder outlining architecture decisions and key trade-offs made during implementation.

Please let me know if any of these assumptions differ from your expectations — I’m happy to adjust accordingly.

This PR addresses a critical security vulnerability where user PINs were stored in plaintext in the database.

Changes:
- **Hashing:** Implemented PBKDF2 (100,000 iterations, SHA256) for PIN storage.
- **Verification:** Updated login flow to verify hashes instead of plaintext comparison.
- **Management:** Updated user creation/editing to hash PINs.
- **Seeding:** Updated seed data in `AppDbContext` and migrations to use hashed values for default users (Admin: 0000, Barbero 1: 1111, Barbero 2: 2222).
- **API Security:** The admin API now returns `****` instead of the PIN hash to prevent offline attacks.

This ensures that even if the database is compromised, user credentials remain protected.

## Summary

Replace bare `except:` with `except ValueError:` in `locomo_benchmark.py` date parsing.

author: therajanmaurya
body:
## Summary

- Add `launchIO` helper function to `BaseViewModel` that launches coroutines on `Dispatchers.Default`
- Prevents UI freezing when performing network or database operations by ensuring they run on background threads

## Problem

When using `viewModelScope.launch { }` without specifying a dispatcher, coroutines run on `Dispatchers.Main` by default. This causes the UI to freeze while waiting for API responses, even if the repository layer uses `withContext(Dispatchers.IO)`, because the coroutine resumes on the Main thread.

## Solution

Add a `launchIO` helper function that all ViewModels inheriting from `BaseViewModel` can use:

```kotlin
protected fun launchIO(block: suspend CoroutineScope.() -> Unit): Job {
    return viewModelScope.launch(Dispatchers.Default, block = block)
}
```

**Note:** Uses `Dispatchers.Default` instead of `Dispatchers.IO` for multiplatform compatibility. `IO` dispatcher is only available on JVM/Android/Native targets, not on JavaScript/WasmJS.

## Usage

Replace:
```kotlin
viewModelScope.launch {
    val result = repository.makeApiCall()
    // UI frozen while waiting
}
```

With:
```kotlin
launchIO {
    val result = repository.makeApiCall()
    // Runs on background thread, UI stays responsive
}
```

## Why This Works

- `StateFlow.update {}` is thread-safe and can be called from any thread
- Compose's `collectAsStateWithLifecycle()` automatically observes on Main thread
- Event channels handle cross-thread communication properly
- `Dispatchers.Default` provides background thread execution on all KMP targets

## Test plan

- [x] Build project successfully (all platforms including Web)
- [ ] Verify existing ViewModels continue to work
- [ ] Update ViewModels to use `launchIO` for I/O operations

author: copilot
body:
The lossy bisection used p95 over **all sampled pixels**. For typical R plots (~98% white background), the 95th percentile was always 0, so the algorithm accepted a single-color palette for any threshold — producing a ~143-byte flat image even at `lossy = 0.01`.

```r
tinypng(tmp, paste0(tmp, "-lossy.png"), lossy = 2.3)
# before: 143 bytes (single flat color)
# after:  3628 bytes (correct palette reduction)
```

## Algorithm change

**Before:** p95 of DeltaE over all ~53k uniformly-sampled pixels. Background pixels (98%+) contributed zeros, drowning out content pixels.

**After:** pixels are grouped by their original RGBA color; the worst-case DeltaE is recorded per unique color; p95 is taken over those per-color values. Every distinct color (axis line, text, data point) gets one equal vote regardless of pixel frequency.

## Evaluation vs. output dithering

Bisection evaluates candidates with `ditherer::None` (nearest-color mapping), which gives a deterministic, monotone DeltaE per unique color. The final output still uses `ditherer::Ordered` for visual quality.

## Bisection performance

Three optimizations speed up the bisection:

1. **Early exit**: quantize at 256 colors first (no dithering) and evaluate the metric. If even 256 colors exceeds the threshold, use 256 immediately — no bisection needed.
2. **Tighter search range**: count the distinct colors actually used in the 256-quantized image and use that count as `hi` instead of always starting at 256, shortening the bisection for images with few unique colors.
3. **No per-step heap allocation**: RGBA keys for sampled pixels are pre-computed once into a `Vec<u32>` before the bisection begins. The `HashMap<u32, f64>` is allocated once and passed as `&mut` into each evaluation step, where `.clear()` (retaining capacity) replaces a full reallocation each iteration.

## Regression test

Added an assertion that `lossy = 2.3` output exceeds 500 bytes, guarding against a recurrence of the single-color collapse.

author: sanyon1
body: ### Dear Maintainer, I am submitting this PR to address a bug where the UITextEllipsisOverflow component permanently clears the text when it is initialized within dynamic layout systems (such as GridLayoutGroup). ### Summary of Changes > Before Fix: There was an issue where labels were cleared if the number of buttons added to a ButtonCollection was 2 or fewer. > After Fix: Labels are preserved and displayed correctly regardless of the button count. ### How to Reproduce In [DefaultCellDemoDebugPage.cs](https://github.com/Haruma-K/UnityDebugSheet/blob/2b1cf90f0375e10c9c0909cc91c5b92d707f2ce3/Assets/Demo/02_DefaultCells/Scripts/DefaultCellsDemoDebugPage.cs#L210), simply change line 210 from for (var i = 0; i < 9; i++) to for (var i = 0; i < 2; i++). ### The Problem The issue stems from a timing conflict between text assignment and layout initialization: 1. Assignment: New text is assigned to the component (e.g., during a cell's Setup). 2. Premature Truncation: The component immediately runs its Apply() logic using the initial dimensions of the RectTransform. 3. Data Loss: If these initial dimensions have not yet been properly calculated by the layout engine, the component determines that there is insufficient space and begins removing characters from the text one by one from the end, eventually removing them all. 4. Layout Initialization: When the layout is subsequently initialized and the dimensions are updated, the original text is already lost, leaving the UI element empty. ### The Solution I have updated the component to decouple the Original Text (Source of Truth) from the Display Output: - The component now preserves the original string whenever a new value is assigned. - It always uses this preserved original text as the starting point for truncation. - This allows the component to correctly re-calculate the ellipsis during OnRectTransformDimensionsChange once the layout initialization is complete. This change ensures that text remains visible and correctly truncated regardless of whether the ellipsis logic triggers before or after the layout engine provides the final dimensions.

author: debu-sinha
body:
Closes #9164

## What changes are proposed

This PR adds a JSON-based save/load path that avoids cloudpickle entirely, addressing CVE concerns with untrusted `.pkl` files. Users can now save and load DSPy programs without any pickle involvement:

```python
# Save
module.save("my_model", save_program=True, safe=True)

# Load (no allow_pickle needed)
loaded = dspy.load("my_model")
```

The safe format stores:
- `metadata.json` with `"format": "safe_v1"` for auto-detection
- `program.json` with the module class, sub-module tree, and full state

On load, modules are reconstructed via `object.__new__()` + `_base_init()` + `load_state()`, following the same pattern as PyTorch's `state_dict`.

### Key changes

**Signature serialization** (`dspy/signatures/signature.py`):
- `dump_state()` now emits field metadata: `name`, `field_type` (input/output), and `type` (serialized Python type annotation)
- `load_state()` has three paths: (1) update in-place when field names match, (2) reconstruct from scratch when fields differ (safe load path), (3) legacy format backward compat
- Added `_type_to_str()` / `_str_to_type()` for round-tripping Python type annotations through JSON

**Predict config** (`dspy/predict/predict.py`):
- `dump_state()` now includes `config` (temperature, max_tokens, etc.)
- `load_state()` restores config with backward compat for older state dicts

**Module tree** (`dspy/primitives/base_module.py`):
- Added `_collect_module_tree()` that walks `__dict__` recursively to record sub-module paths and classes (handles attributes, lists, dicts)
- Added `safe=True` parameter to `save()` which writes `program.json` + `metadata.json` instead of `program.pkl`

**Safe loading** (`dspy/utils/saving.py`):
- `dspy.load()` auto-detects `safe_v1` format from metadata and loads without requiring `allow_pickle`
- `_reconstruct_module()` creates modules via `object.__new__()`, wires the sub-module tree, then calls `load_state()`
- Handles bracketed paths like `layers[0].predict` and `modules['key']`
- Legacy cloudpickle format continues to work unchanged

### Backward compatibility

- Existing `save_program=True` (without `safe=True`) behavior is unchanged
- `load_state()` handles both new enhanced format and legacy format transparently
- `dspy.load()` auto-detects format; legacy `.pkl` models still work with `allow_pickle=True`

## How is this PR tested

27 new tests in `tests/utils/test_safe_saving.py`:
- Type serialization round-trips (str, int, list[str], dict[str, int], etc.)
- Signature dump/load with field metadata (in-place update, reconstruction from scratch, legacy compat)
- Predict config serialization and backward compat
- Safe save file structure validation
- Full round-trip for ChainOfThought, Predict, and nested custom modules
- Version mismatch warnings
- Error cases (missing class, non-directory path)

All 41 existing signature tests pass. All 13 relevant base_module tests pass.

author: copilot
body:
Two targeted, measurable improvements — one performance (LCP), one discovery (social sharing).

## Performance: LCP — first episode image (`EpisodeList.astro`)

Every episode image was `loading="lazy"`, including the first one, which is the above-the-fold LCP candidate on the homepage. Lazy-loading it defers the fetch until after viewport detection, adding a full render cycle to the LCP time.

```astro
// Before — all images treated equally
loading="lazy"

// After — first image prioritized, rest unchanged
loading={index === 0 ? 'eager' : 'lazy'}
fetchpriority={index === 0 ? 'high' : 'auto'}
```

**Measure:** Lighthouse on the homepage — LCP time decreases because the first episode thumbnail is fetched in parallel with HTML parsing rather than after layout.

## Discovery: Twitter/X card type (`Layout.astro`)

```astro
// Before
<meta content="summary" name="twitter:card" />

// After
<meta content="summary_large_image" name="twitter:card" />
```

`summary_large_image` occupies ~4× the visual area in Twitter/X feeds versus `summary`. **Measure:** Twitter Card Validator before/after; quantitative CTR via Vercel Analytics on shared episode URLs.

## Tests

E2e tests updated to assert:
- First episode image: `loading="eager"`, `fetchpriority="high"`
- Subsequent images: `loading="lazy"`
- All pages: `twitter:card` = `summary_large_image`

author: markdumay
body:
Layer 1: set window.ckySettings.iframeSupport = true before any user interaction. CookieYes reads this flag inside _ckySetCookie and switches the consent cookie from SameSite=Strict to SameSite=None;Secure. Without this, the cookie is silently blocked in every cross-site iframe context; CookieYes then re-reads the cookie to verify the write and, finding nothing, keeps the banner open indefinitely.

Layer 2: keep the pointerdown → requestStorageAccess() handler for browsers that block all third-party cookies regardless of SameSite (Firefox Strict, Safari ITP, Chrome with third-party cookies disabled). The Promise resolves as a microtask before CookieYes writes on the subsequent click. The 500 ms reload fallback is removed because Layer 1 already guarantees the write succeeds under Chrome's current defaults, and the reload was causing the banner to reappear.

author: copilot
body:
Comprehensive audit of the `orn` crate to surface bugs, API design problems, missing features, performance gaps, and improvement suggestions. Each finding is captured as a standalone `issues/NN-*.md` file with enough context for an agent with no prior knowledge to act on it independently.

## Confirmed Bugs

- **`ExactSizeIterator` contract violation** (`01`) — `iter::Iterator` overrides `len()` correctly but never overrides `size_hint()`, which returns `(0, None)`. Verified experimentally: `len=3`, `size_hint=(0, None)`. Breaks `collect`, `extend`, `zip` pre-allocation.

## API Design Issues

- **`map_with` tuple argument** (`02`) — closure signature is `FnOnce((S, T)) -> U` instead of the idiomatic `FnOnce(S, T) -> U`; named functions can't be passed directly
- **`as_ref` shadows `AsRef<T>` trait** (`05`) — inherent method wins method resolution; `AsRef::<str>::as_ref(&or)` requires UFCS
- **Inherent `into()` not a trait impl** (`14`) — can't satisfy `T: Into<U>` bounds with it
- **`At<I>` inconsistent return types** (`17`) — returns `Tk` for tuples, `Option<Tk>` for `Or`; can't write uniform generic code over both
- **Derived `Ord` is surprising and undocumented** (`19`) — `T0(999) < T1(0)` always, variant index wins

## Missing Features / Traits

- **`From<Tk>` for each variant** (`03`) — can't write `42u8.into()` or use `Into<Or2<u8,u16>>` bounds
- **`TryFrom<OrN>` for each variant** (`04`) — no standard fallible extraction; `?` propagation impossible
- **`Default`** (`06`) — natural impl: `Or::T0(T0::default())`
- **`Display`** (`07`) — delegates to active variant; `Debug` exists but `{}` doesn't compile
- **`Error` trait** (`10`) — `Or<E0,E1>` can't be used as an error type or boxed as `dyn Error`
- **`unwrap_t0()` / `expect_t0("msg")`** (`11`) — no panic-on-wrong-variant convenience methods
- **`Or1` ↔ `T` conversions** (`13`) — isomorphic to `T`, but neither `From<T>` nor `From<Or1<T>>` exists
- **`Or0` missing all standard derives** (`15`) — bare `enum Or {}` with no `Clone/Debug/PartialEq/…`
- **`widen` / `narrow`** (`18`) — no way to inject `Or2<A,B>` into `Or3<A,B,C>` or project back
- **`fmt::Write` / `io::Write`** (`20`) — can't use `Or<Writer1, Writer2>` as a unified write target

## Performance

- **Missing `fold`, `for_each`, `nth`, `nth_back`, `rfold`** (`08`) — inner-iterator specializations (SIMD folds, O(1) nth) are bypassed; all iteration falls back to repeated `next()` calls

## Documentation / Hygiene

- **Serde wire format undocumented** (`09`) — `Or2::T0(42)` → `{"T0":42}`; stability of variant names as serialized keys is unspecified
- **`rayon::One` is an undocumented `pub` type** (`12`) — Rayon plumbing detail leaks into public API surface
- **`#[must_use]` absent on all pure methods** (`16`) — discarding `.t0()`, `.map_t0()`, `.is_t0()` etc. is silent

## Suggestions

- **`std::ops` integrations** (`21`) — `Index`/`IndexMut`, unary/binary arithmetic for uniform `Or<T,T,…,T>`
- **`partition_or` combinator** (`22`) — split `Iterator<Item=Or2<A,B>>` into `(Vec<A>, Vec<B>)` in one pass
- **Proc-macro companion crate** (`23`) — `#[into_or]` for automatic `map_err` variant selection in `Result`-returning functions

Promotes `MessageList.tsx` from a legacy stub into the canonical message display component, adds the two missing issue requirements (date separators + loading skeleton), and fixes scroll/ghosting bugs discovered during review.

### Scroll fixes
- `useLayoutEffect` (fires before paint) instead of `useEffect` for initial bottom-scroll → no visible scroll animation on channel load
- Instant `scrollTop = scrollHeight` on mount; smooth `scrollIntoView` only for new messages while already near bottom

---

- [x] Messages render from mock data in chronological order
- [x] Author grouping works correctly (compact mode, same-day guard)
- [x] Date separators appear between calendar-day boundaries

## Summary

This PR introduces a lens-aware screenshot architecture that enables isolated two-phase analysis when a 15M ICT indicator overlay is provided. The system now enforces a hard cap of 4 screenshots (3 clean price charts + 1 optional overlay) and uses separate API calls to prevent model anchoring on indicator data during the clean price baseline phase.

## Key Changes

### Core Architecture
- **ScreenshotMetadata model**: New typed evidence metadata for each screenshot with validation rules:
  - Clean price charts must have `lens="NONE"` and `evidence_type="price_only"`
  - Overlay charts must have `lens="ICT"` and `evidence_type="indicator_overlay"` with required `indicator_claims`
  - Enforces mutual exclusivity between lens types and evidence types

- **GroundTruthPacket enhancements**:
  - Added `screenshot_metadata` list (one entry per clean chart)
  - Added `m15_overlay` and `m15_overlay_metadata` optional fields for the 15M ICT overlay
  - Added model validator enforcing: max 4 total screenshots, allowed timeframes (H4/H1/M15/M5), metadata count matching charts count
  - Metadata must accompany every clean chart; overlay metadata required when overlay is provided

### Two-Phase Analysis Pipeline
- **Phase 1 (mandatory)**: `parallel_analyst_node` runs all analysts against clean price charts only
  - Prompt explicitly states "CLEAN PRICE ANALYSIS ONLY" and forbids anticipating overlays
  - Analysts must explicitly state what cannot be determined from price alone

- **Phase 2 (conditional)**: New `overlay_delta_node` runs only when 15M overlay is provided
  - Each analyst receives its own Phase 1 output as context
  - Uses separate API calls with isolated context to prevent anchoring
  - Produces `OverlayDeltaReport` with four structured fields: `confirms`, `refines`, `contradicts`, `indicator_only_claims`

- **Conditional routing**: Pipeline branches after Phase 1 based on `ground_truth.m15_overlay` presence

### Analyst Output & Verdict Updates
- **OverlayDeltaReport**: New schema for structured overlay delta analysis with all four fields required (empty lists valid)
- **ApprovedSetup**: Added `indicator_dependent` boolean flag to track setups relying primarily on indicator claims
- **FinalVerdict**: Added overlay-related fields:
  - `overlay_was_provided`: boolean flag
  - `indicator_dependent`: boolean flag
  - `indicator_dependency_notes`: optional string
  - `AuditLog` extended with `overlay_provided` and `indicator_dependent_setups` count

### API & UI Updates
- **API endpoint** (`/analyse`):
  - Updated to accept clean charts (H4, H1, M15, M5) and optional 15M overlay
  - Added overlay metadata fields: `overlay_indicator_source`, `overlay_settings_locked`, `overlay_indicator_claims`
  - Constructs `ScreenshotMetadata` for each clean chart and overlay
  - Validates architecture constraints before creating GroundTruthPacket

- **Frontend** (`app/index.html`, `form_bindings.js`):
  - Reorganized chart upload UI to emphasize clean price charts
  - Added progressive disclosure toggle for optional 15M ICT overlay slot
  - Updated descriptions to clarify lens-aware architecture

### Prompt & Arbiter Updates
- **Analyst prompt builder**: 
  - `build_analyst_prompt()` now explicitly marks Phase 1 and forbids overlay anticipation
  - New `build_overlay_delta_prompt()` for Phase 2 with isolated context
  - Output schema updated with explicit uncertainty guidance for clean analysis

- **Arbiter prompt builder**:
  - Injects overlay delta reports when provided
  - Applies lens-aware weighting rules for agreement, refinement, contradiction, and indicator-only claims
  - Marks overlay section clearly in prompt

- Comprehensive test suite added for:

author: costajohnt
body:
## Summary

- **Rewrites the rendering pipeline from PNG screenshots to SVG extraction** with post-render measurement via `getBBox()` and width-first scaling
- **Simplifies the MCP server to a thin CLI wrapper** that delegates all rendering to the CLI via `execFile`, eliminating the duplicate rendering pipeline
- **Bundles mermaid.js locally** (v11.12.3) for offline support and version pinning, removing CDN dependency

## What changed

**Core pipeline:**
- Mermaid diagrams are now rendered to SVG strings (not PNG) with exact dimensions measured via `getBBox()`
- Width-first scaling: diagrams scale to fit page width (never upscale), with a 60% minimum scale floor
- Tall diagrams overflow across pages naturally instead of being squeezed
- `useMaxWidth: false` on all 15 diagram types eliminates whitespace bloat

**New/rewritten files:**
- `src/types.ts` — shared type definitions (`PageSize`, `ConversionOptions`, `RenderedDiagram`, etc.)
- `src/converter.ts` — main pipeline: parse → render → size → assemble HTML → PDF
- `src/mermaidRenderer.ts` — SVG extraction with singleton browser and race-condition-safe launch
- `src/diagramCache.ts` — theme-aware SHA-256 cache for rendered SVGs
- `src/cli.ts` — stdin support, argument validation, 30s stdin timeout

**Removed:**
- `src/finalConverter.ts` (replaced by `converter.ts`)
- `src/browserPool.ts` (singleton browser in renderer)
- `mermaid-to-pdf-mcp/src/diagramAnalyzer.ts` (measurement replaces estimation)
- MCP duplicate rendering pipeline, CDN loading, `scale: 0.9`, `max-height: 400px`

**Security & robustness (4 rounds of automated review, 41 findings fixed):**
- `execFile` over `exec` (command injection prevention)
- `securityLevel: 'strict'` in mermaid config
- Input size limits (50KB mermaid, 10MB markdown)
- Runtime validation at all trust boundaries
- CRLF line ending support, non-.md extension safety
- Immutable shared constants (`as const`, `Object.freeze`)

## Test plan

- [ ] `npm test` — 16 unit tests pass (CLI, converter, cache, renderer)
- [ ] `npm run test:e2e` — 3 end-to-end tests with real mermaid documents
- [ ] Manual: `markdown-mermaid-converter test-fixtures/sample.md` produces clean PDF
- [ ] Manual: `cat test-fixtures/sample.md | markdown-mermaid-converter -o /tmp/piped.pdf`
- [ ] Manual: Verify diagrams scale correctly (no horizontal overflow, no excessive whitespace)

### Motivation
- Improve vector/Bézier editing UX by adding per-node controls, node-type transformations (corner/smooth/mirrored), and multi-anchor editing. 
- Make creation and preview of Bézier paths more robust to dragging, pending-closing, and transform changes. 
- Persist vector model state in serialization/history and keep the vector model in sync when paths are moved or transformed.

### Description
- Added a new UI panel (`#vectorNodePanel`) and controls (`btnNodeCorner`, `btnNodeSmooth`, `btnNodeMirrored`, `btnNodeBreak`) to display and edit selected anchor nodes and their types. 
- Implemented node model helpers and behaviors including `normalizeBezierPointKind`, `inferAnchorDisplayType`, `selectBezierAnchorIndices`, `applySelectedNodeType`, `toggleSelectedNodeBreak`, and `applyAnchorCoupling` to support corner/smooth/mirrored anchors and coupled handle motion. 
- Improved Bézier creation flow with drag thresholds, pending-close behavior, preview improvements using command-style paths (`bezierPointsToPathCommands`), safer preview updates, and functions `finalizeBezierPendingClose`, `resetCreatePointToCorner`, and refined `addBezierPoint`/`updateDraggedCreatePoint`. 
- Enhanced editor controls and interactions: control creation/positioning scaling, single-click anchor toggling, multi-select anchors (Shift), insertion/removal of points (`insertPointOnSegment`, `removePointAtIndex`), and updated mouse/key handlers to better coordinate `bezier`, `direct-select`, and `select` tools. 
- Added vector model tracking and sync helpers (`trackPathPosition`, `syncPathVectorModelByDelta`, `refreshObjectCoords`) and included `vectorModel` in the serialized properties via `SERIALIZE_PROPS`, plus hooked syncing on `object:modified` and during movement to preserve model coordinates after transforms. 
- Miscellaneous polish: handle visual scaling, handle radii getters, status messages, and safety around path parsing and preview failures.

### Testing
- Ran the project's linting and JavaScript unit/integration test suite locally and confirmed no regressions in automated tests. 
- Executed automated canvas/object lifecycle hooks (object add/modify/remove) and headless smoke checks for save/load/undo/redo flows, which completed successfully.

### Motivation
- Prevent 500-level crashes when building response headers that contain non-latin1 characters (Thai) by ensuring all header values are Latin-1/ASCII-safe while still supporting UTF-8 filenames via RFC 5987 encoding.

### Description
- Added `toAsciiFilename(...)` to sanitize a safe ASCII fallback filename for `filename="..."` usage in `Content-Disposition`.
- Added `buildContentDisposition(asciiName, utf8Name?)` to emit an ASCII fallback and an RFC 5987 `filename*=UTF-8''...` percent-encoded UTF-8 filename when provided.
- Switched the download response to use `NextResponse` and set `Content-Disposition` via the helper, and added `Cache-Control: no-store` for the generated document response.
- Added a dev-only console log that prints the final `Content-Disposition` value and a boolean `hasOnlyAsciiOrPercentEncoding` check to validate header safety during development, and kept error responses as JSON so Thai text never appears in headers/statusText.

author: copilot
body:
Creates a full waiter order-taking app targeting Android and browser, built with Ionic 8, Angular 19, Capacitor 7, and Bootstrap 5.3. All code uses standalone components, Angular signals, `@if`/`@for` control flow, and `inject()` throughout — no NgModules, no `*ngIf`/`*ngFor`, no constructor injection.

## Project scaffold (`waiterordering/`)

- **`package.json`** — Ionic 8, Angular 19, Capacitor 7 (`@capacitor/{android,device,app,keyboard,status-bar,haptics}`), Bootstrap 5.3, RxJS 7.8, TypeScript 5.6
- **`capacitor.config.ts`** — App ID `io.waiterordering.starter`, `webDir: www`
- **`angular.json`** — build via `@angular-devkit/build-angular:application`; `serve.options.proxyConfig: "proxy.conf.js"`
- **`proxy.conf.js`** — routes `/proxy/*` → `http://{x-target-ip}:5000`, strips `/proxy` prefix, falls back to `127.0.0.1:5000`

## App shell

- **`main.ts`** — `bootstrapApplication` with `provideHttpClient()`, `provideRouter(..., withPreloading(PreloadAllModules))`, `importProvidersFrom(IonicModule.forRoot())`, `IonicRouteStrategy`
- **`app.routes.ts`** — lazy `loadComponent` for `/login`, `/selectTable`, `/menu`; root redirects to `/login`
- **`app.component.ts`** — standalone root with `IonRouterOutlet` + `HeaderComponent`

## Services

- **`OrderService`** — auto-detects native vs. browser; uses `/proxy/api/v1` + `x-target-ip` header on web, `http://{ip}:5000/api/v1` on Android. `loginUser()` iterates all URL/payload variants before throwing with `triedUrls`:

```typescript
// Tries /api/v1/checkUser, /api/v1/checkuser, /checkUser, /checkuser
// × {userName, username} payloads; throws { triedUrls, errors } on total failure
async loginUser(data): Promise<Observable<any>>
```

## Pages & components (all standalone, signals, `@if`/`@for`)

- **`HeaderComponent`** — reacts to `NavigationEnd` via signal; shows route title or `TBNAME` query param
- **`LoginPage`** — two-phase flow: IP connectivity check → credential login; uses `@capacitor/device` for device ID
- **`SelectTablePage`** — loads tables, renders color-coded cards (occupied/available), navigates to `/menu?id=&TBNAME=`
- **`MenuPage`** — category drill-down, per-item qty/remarks, search via `ion-searchbar`; fixed bottom bar for Place Order / View Order
- **`OrderSummaryComponent`** — modal showing previously placed orders (from API) + current session items with inline qty editing

## Styles

- `global.scss` imports `bootstrap/dist/css/bootstrap.min.css`; `theme/variables.scss` sets Ionic CSS custom properties

body:
Previous attempt only committed an empty plan. This implements the actual AI features for the platform.

## New AI Services

### `recommendation_service.py` — Content-based filtering
- `get_similar_products(id, n)` — similarity scored as weighted sum of category (45%), price-bucket (25%), and Jaccard text overlap (30%)
- `get_recommendations(user_id, n)` — personalised picks excluding already-viewed/purchased items, boosted by category affinity from purchase history
- `get_trending(n, category)` — popularity ranking: purchases weight 3×, views weight 1×
- `record_view()` / `record_purchase()` — interaction tracking

### `styling_service.py` — Outfit composition engine
- `suggest_outfit(product, pool, max_items)` — "Complete the look" using domain rules (top→bottom+footwear+accessory, dress→footwear+outerwear, etc.)
- `score_outfit_compatibility(p1, p2)` — 0–1 score: category rules (50%) + style label compatibility (30%) + colour-family compatibility (20%)
- `get_style_profile(purchase_history)` — returns preferred categories, styles, colours, avg spend

```python
svc = StylingService()
tee = Product(1, "White Tee", "top", 29.99, style="casual", color="white")
outfit = svc.suggest_outfit(tee, available_products, max_items=4)
# → [Blue Jeans (bottom), White Sneakers (footwear), Canvas Tote (accessory)]
```

## New API Endpoints

| Method | Path | Auth | Description |
|--------|------|------|-------------|
| `GET` | `/api/v1/recommendations` | JWT | Personalised picks |
| `GET` | `/api/v1/products/<id>/similar` | — | Similar products |
| `GET` | `/api/v1/trending` | — | Trending (optional `?category=`) |
| `POST` | `/api/v1/recommendations/record-view` | JWT | Record view event |
| `GET` | `/api/v1/styling/outfit` | — | Outfit suggestions for `?product_id=` |
| `GET` | `/api/v1/styling/profile` | JWT | Style profile from purchase history |

Categories are inferred from product name/description at query time via the styling engine, so the existing Product ORM (which has no explicit category column) feeds correctly into both AI services.

## Supporting Infrastructure

- **Standalone in-memory service modules** (`user_service_simple`, `product_service_simple`, `order_service_simple`) implementing the interfaces expected by the pre-existing unit tests, which previously had no backing implementation

author: notsuhas
body:
## Summary
This fixes a non-loop `scrollTo({ index })` regression where navigating backward could produce a positive offset and briefly render a blank item/state.

## User Impact
In `v5.0.0-beta.4`, when `loop={false}` and a consumer computes a previous index manually (for example with modulo arithmetic) then calls `scrollTo({ index: prevIndex, animated: false })`, some transitions can land in an invalid offset direction. That can surface as a blank frame/item.

`v5.0.0-beta.0` did not show this behavior in the same usage pattern.

## Root Cause
`useCarouselController` used loop-style direction math inside `to()` for both loop and non-loop modes. In non-loop mode, moving to a lower target index could flip direction and compute a positive final offset.

## Fix
In non-loop mode, `scrollTo({ index })` now uses direct page mapping:
- `finalOffset = -index * size`

Loop mode keeps existing direction and wrap behavior.

## Tests
Added regression coverage in `useCarouselController.test.tsx`:
- `should keep negative offsets when scrollTo() moves backward in non-loop mode`
- `should map scrollTo({ index: 0 }) to zero offset from end in non-loop mode`

Also re-ran the existing non-loop left-overscroll integration check in `Carousel.test.tsx` (targeted test).

## Validation Run
- `yarn test src/hooks/useCarouselController.test.tsx --runInBand --watchman=false`
- `yarn test src/components/Carousel.test.tsx -t "left overscroll" --runInBand --watchman=false`
